rationale: All four prior blocking findings were graded against source at HEAD inside budget: CR-001 (the effect now calls getAuthCallbackAcceptanceMs(resolvedHintMs) at :193 and the dead AUTH_CALLBACK_HINT_MS export is gone, with no other importer of the changed signature), CR-003 (a substantive chat retry pin at chatGeneration.promptAuth.test.ts:245 drives two distinct initiate calls and asserts the consumed auth_url is never reopened) and CR-004 (one isLateCallbackTarget serves both success and rollback, matching the user's explicit override of spec.md, pinned on a rolled-back row and on an already-authenticated row) are resolved. CR-002 is not: the scrutinized exemption is safe on unmount, but once the hint-expiry rollback has dropped the id from trackedAuthConfigIds no later cancel, clearRows or chat switch produces an untrack transition at all, and retention is purged only at acceptance expiry, on re-track, on callback arrival or on unmount - so an abandoned flow still beacons result:'timeout' at 600 s and useChatAuthCallbacks routes a late success at whichever chat is then open, both sentences from CR-002's original problem statement still true at HEAD and no test covering cancel-after-hint-expiry. The confirmation pass's blind and edge-case lenses both returned parseable output and surfaced no new security, public-API, data-loss or build/runtime-correctness issue, so no finding was added; business_review and standards_review are carried forward unchanged and standards_path is null by contract on a check round.

findings.title: Retention survives a post-hint-expiry cancel or chat switch
findings.problem: Narrowed to the residue after commit 29359c919, which did fix the two headline paths: an id untracked before its hint fires now has its acceptance timer cleared (:232-234), and a re-track clears the previous attempt's hint and acceptance handles plus its retention before arming new ones (:254-256). What remains is the exemption the fix-up was asked to justify. Retention is purged in exactly four places - acceptance expiry (:219), re-track (:256), callback arrival (:337) and the unmount reset (:374) - and the untrack branch never purges it at all. Because the hint expiry's own rollback drops the row out of isAuthenticatingGateRow (utils/mcpAuth.ts:50-53), the id leaves trackedAuthConfigIds on the very next render, so a cancel, clearRows or chat switch that happens afterwards produces no untrack transition for that id and reaches none of the four purge routes: the 600 s acceptance timer stays armed and the id stays retained unconditionally. Unmount is the one case the exemption cannot leak through, since the cleanup effect (:365-377) clears both maps and resets both sets. A cancel racing the rollback render additionally enters the exemption branch directly. No test covers cancel-after-hint-expiry; the new case at useAuthCallbackListener.test.tsx:482 covers only untracking before the hint fires.
findings.impact: Two sentences from this finding's original problem statement are still literally true at HEAD. (a) An abandoned flow still POSTs result:'timeout' at its acceptance deadline for a sign-in the user cancelled or walked away from, polluting the EPMCDME-14226 metric - the audited one-beacon-per-id-at-acceptance-expiry constraint itself holds, since the beacon fires once and never at hint expiry, but the record is false. (b) Retention is a single module-level ref shared across chats while useChatAuthCallbacks rebinds its handlers to currentChat.id on every switch (useChatAuthCallbacks.ts:50-51), so a late success for chat A arriving after the user moved to chat B is dispatched as markPromptAuthSuccess(chatB.id, ...): it no-ops if chat B has no row for that auth_config_id, leaving chat A's row stuck on the hint copy, or - because the success matcher now accepts any row that is not authenticated - lands on chat B's row for the same MCP server instead. Either way AC 1 fails on the chat-switch path, which is this ticket's own defect recurring.
findings.recommendation: Purging on untrack cannot fix this, and removing the exemption would break AC 3 / AC 5 exactly as the implementer reasoned - the problem is that no untrack transition exists to hook by the time the user cancels or switches. Give retention an explicit end: either have consumers signal abandonment (an untrackAuthConfigId / abandon callback the cancel and clearRows paths call, which purges both stages), or scope each retained entry to the context that created it - store the originating chat id alongside the id and dispatch a late callback through the handler captured at track time rather than the current ref, so a chat switch can neither lose nor misroute it. Then add the two missing cases to useAuthCallbackListener.test.tsx with navigator.sendBeacon stubbed: cancel after a hint expiry sends no beacon and accepts no late callback, and a chat switch after a hint expiry still applies the late success to the originating chat.

finding_status.notes: useAuthCallbackListener.ts:193 now reads `const resolvedAcceptanceMs = getAuthCallbackAcceptanceMs(resolvedHintMs)`, so the helper the AC 2 tests exercise is the one production runs; the helper takes hintMs explicitly (:118-119) and hintMs is still validated upstream by getPositiveInteger via getAuthCallbackHintMs (:97-114). AUTH_CALLBACK_HINT_MS is gone from both the module body and the export list (:382-388), and a repo-wide grep shows the changed getAuthCallbackAcceptanceMs signature has no importer outside this module and its test, so the widened signature breaks no caller. A rendered-hook pin was added at useAuthCallbackListener.test.tsx:684 alongside the two helper assertions.

Partially addressed, not resolved. Fixed: the untrack branch now clears the acceptance timer for a non-retained id (:232-234), and the re-track path clears both handles and the stale retention before arming (:254-256), which closes the false beacon for a pre-hint untrack and the retried-id double beacon; tests at :482, :515, :568 and :598 cover those and the unmount case, and the timing in the retry test is sound because the acceptance timer is armed at track time (:262), not at hint expiry. Not fixed - and this is the exemption the caller asked to be scrutinized: it is safe only for unmount, where the cleanup effect (:365-377) clears both maps unconditionally. For cancel, clearRows and chat switch the exemption is reachable, and worse, usually bypassed entirely: the hint-expiry rollback already drops the id from trackedAuthConfigIds (isAuthenticatingGateRow requires status === 'authenticating'), so a later cancel or chat switch produces no untrack transition at all and none of the four retention purge routes (:219, :256, :337, :374) is reached. The acceptance timer keeps running and beacons a false 'timeout', and retention plus the rebound useChatAuthCallbacks handlers (useChatAuthCallbacks.ts:50-51) misroute a late success to whichever chat is then open. No test covers cancel-after-hint-expiry.

chatGeneration.promptAuth.test.ts:245 adds 're-runs initiate after a hint expiry rollback and never reuses a consumed auth_url'. The pin is substantive rather than nominal: it drives initiate + continue for attempt 1, rolls the row back through rollbackPromptAuthRow with the hint copy, then drives the retry and asserts two initiate POSTs, that the last window.open used the second attempt's auth_url and not the consumed first, and that pending_initiate is null. The in-file comment records the no-production-change verdict the finding's recommendation explicitly permitted.

The decision was made and implemented: chatGeneration.ts:301 defines one isLateCallbackTarget (row.status !== 'authenticated') and both markPromptAuthSuccess (:947) and rollbackPromptAuthRow (:958) use it, so a late identity-provider error now reaches a chat row the hint expiry already rolled back, guarded so an authenticated row is never clobbered. Graded against the user's explicit override of spec.md's narrow-rollback line, as directed, not against spec.md. Both halves are pinned in chatGeneration.promptAuth.test.ts - 'lands a late identity-provider error on a row the hint expiry already rolled back' (:188) and 'does not let rollbackPromptAuthRow clobber an already authenticated row' (:205) - which is what this finding's recommendation required. The widening's side effects raised by the confirmation lenses (a rollback matching a config_error or discovery_failed row, or the newest of two rows sharing an auth_config_id) fall outside the check round's new-finding bar and are noted here rather than emitted.
